components.name: Neon Tube Word
components.description: Signature: a word bent as a tube (spill, tube, core). The real build uses EMS Allure single-stroke paths from src/neon-glyphs.ts; this snippet shows the three-layer construction on a simple stroke.
components.css: .ds-neon { display: block; width: 220px; height: auto; overflow: visible; } .ds-neon path { fill: none; stroke-linecap: round; stroke-linejoin: round; } .ds-neon__spill path { stroke: #ff3045; stroke-width: 14; opacity: 0.16; } .ds-neon__tube path { stroke: #ff3045; stroke-width: 5.4; } .ds-neon__core path { stroke: #ffd5d9; stroke-width: 1.7; opacity: 0.95; } .ds-neon:hover .ds-neon__tube path { stroke: rgba(237,231,223,0.15); } .ds-neon:hover .ds-neon__spill path { opacity: 0; } .ds-neon:hover .ds-neon__core path { stroke: rgba(255,255,255,0.28); }

narrative.overview:
A dark room wall at night, warm black with faint plaster grain, carrying one continuous hand-bent neon circuit. Neon red is the gas for signs and for the action; argon cobalt is the gas for live numbers. Everything that is not lit is either the wall, clear unlit glass, or the hardware that holds glass to a wall: electrode sleeves, standoff clips, hooks and feed wires. Display words are not set in a font; they are single-stroke script (EMS Allure, drawn as tube paths) bent as tubes with a light spill, a coloured tube and a white-hot core.

The page reads like signage rather than a product brochure: Barlow Semi Condensed carries statements in road-sign plainness, Barlow carries reading, and the neon script carries the one phrase per heading that the visitor should remember. Density is low; each section is one sign and its spec plate. Motion is electrical: tubes strike with two failed starts before holding, current travels the circuit on scroll, and reduced motion shows everything lit.

The site is dark by binding brand commitment; even a "brighter" section is only a wall lit a little more (#131012). The red halo-ring logo glows as the only lit part of the header.
keyCharacteristics: One continuous circuit links the hero to every service; services are rows on one rail, never a grid of equal cards.
Light lives only on lit glass and lit controls; panels never glow.
Two gases only: red for signs and action, argon for live numbers.
Unlit is a real state (clear glass with a glint), and lighting up is an event.
Mono appears only on measurements: spec plates, readings, timelines.

rules.name: The Two Gases Rule
rules.body: Red is for signs and the action; argon is for numbers that change with the visitor's input. No third accent colour. The one exception is the WhatsApp icon's green inside the tube button, which is the channel's own mark.

rules.name: The Light On Glass Rule
rules.body: Glow (spill strokes, drop-shadow halos, text-shadow) belongs only to lit glass: neon lettering, the current, the logo ring, lit buttons and argon readings. Panels, plates and cards are never given a coloured glow.

rules.name: The Stays Dark Rule
rules.body: No light theme and no light sections. A section that needs separation uses Lit Wall, a divider line, or more space.

rules.name: The Two-Line Title Rule
rules.body: A section title is a statement line in Barlow Semi Condensed followed by a second line drawn as neon script (about 1.02em tall). The script line is the phrase to remember, kept short enough to bend as one tube.

rules.name: The Mono Measures Rule
rules.body: JetBrains Mono appears only where a value is measured or specified: plate labels, "live in" and "you measure" tags, data sources. It never labels sections or sits above headings.

rules.name: The Drawn Not Typed Rule
rules.body: Neon words are always the Neon component's tube paths, with the real words repeated for screen readers. Never fake neon with a script webfont and text-shadow.

rules.name: The One Rail Rule
rules.body: Sequences (services, results steps) hang on one continuous line with clips or nodes at each stop, divided by thin rules. They are never laid out as a grid of equal boxed cards.

rules.name: The Lit Or Unlit Rule
rules.body: Every tube has exactly three states: off (clear glass, glint, cold tip), igniting (the strike: two failed starts over 0.9s, stepped, then hold), on. Ignition is driven by scroll or arrival; under reduced motion everything is on.

dos: Do draw every display phrase with the Neon component and keep its screen-reader text.
Do give every new tube an off state and let it strike (0.9s stepped) when it comes into view; show it on under reduced motion.
Do keep one lit red button per action group, paired with a tube outline button.
Do hang sequences on one rail with clips or nodes, divided by hairlines.
Do colour numbers that respond to the visitor's input in argon, with tabular numerals.
Do keep the wall dark; separate sections with Lit Wall, a hairline or space.
donts: Don't add a third accent colour or a light section.
Don't put coloured glow on panels, plates or cards; glow is light thrown by lit glass.
Don't fake neon with a script webfont plus text-shadow.
Don't use JetBrains Mono for section labels, eyebrows or anything that is not a measurement.
Don't lay services or steps out as a grid of equal boxed cards.
